what: Play the hero big-text Lottie’s leading intro frames (default 51) once — scroll is locked meanwhile (lock: on, or whoever consumes fx:lock and fx:unlock) — then pin the panel to the top edge of the screen and tie the remaining frames to scroll. Pin length is remaining frames × speed px (default 40 = original slow, minimum 1500px) and ScrollTrigger progress p sets the frame straight to intro + p × remaining frames (linear proportion — the keyframe curve inside Lottie is the scroll curve as is). A hero where text rises from below onto a mask, holds, then on scroll letters bounce up and fly away. wait: play means it loads and plays when the consumer fires fx:play after the loader ends. When playback ends, fx:unlock·fx:done.

options.src: Lottie JSON path (relative to the page using it) or #id — within the document <script type="application/json" id=…> Read when using (file:// pages cannot load files, so use #id). The side that measures fonts to build data is used with wait: play and filled right before fx:play
options.intro: Number of leading frames to autoplay, default 51
options.speed: Scroll px per remaining frame, default 40 (original slow · medium 28 · fast 18)
options.scrub: ScrollTrigger scrub, default 1 (original value — no tween is attached, so the frame follows progress directly)
options.fit: rendererSettings.preserveAspectRatio, default xMaxYMax meet (original — sticks to the bottom right of the board)
options.wait: play — does not play right after attaching, loads and plays when an fx:play event reaches the element (like 2.7s after the loader)
options.lock: on — from attachment until the previous playback ends, html overflow: hidden. When off, only fx:lock and fx:unlock events are fired
options.media: Set up only when this condition holds (e.g. (min-width: 1025px)) — otherwise just release the lock and return (the original does not set up Lottie at 1024 and below)
options.rest: Frame to hold under reduced motion, default intro
options.[data-fx-part=stage]: Child to draw the Lottie in (optional) — if absent, the element itself. What gets pinned is the element itself

from.where: index.html .rx-hero (text Lottie — 1920×1080 · 29.97fps · 139 frames, plays 0–51 after the 2.7s loader and 51–138 at 87×40=3480px fixed scrub). Original layout bundle initScrollLottie, setupScrollTrigger, bindIntroTrigger (introEndFrame 51, speed slow 40, medium 28, fast 18, default 35, Math.max(n×speed, 1500), scrub 1, pin, anticipatePin 1, start top top, and when it ends, remove locked and scrollTo 0).

note: The original loads Lottie, waits for ScrollSmoother, sets the lock 400ms later, and ignores onUpdate until the previous playback ends — here the lock goes up as soon as loading finishes and onUpdate is ignored the same way. Scrolling back to the top (the original unlockScroll scrollTo 0) is left to the consumer in fx:unlock (smooth-scroll builds differ)
